newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore plans major exhibition centre.
newsitem.headline: Singapore plans major exhibition centre.

text.p: Singapore plans to become the largest exhibition venue in Southeast Asia by building an exhibition centre of up to 100,000 sq m (119,600 sq yd), Minister for Trade and Industry Yeo Cheow Tong said on Thursday.

Phase one of the project, which will involve the construction of 60,000 sq m (71,760 sq yds) of covered exhibition space, will cost Singapore $150 million ($107 million), excluding land costs, he told a news conference.

Scheduled for completion in early 1999, phase one will include conference rooms with room for around 2,000 people, 20,000 sq m (23,900 sq yds) of outdoor exhibition space, retail space and other supporting facilities, he said.
Yeo said the government would review the need for phase two, which involves the construction of the remaining 40,000 sq m (47,840 sq yds) according to demand.
He said Cox Richardson Rayner had been appointed project consultant and the Port of Singapore Authority, the agent.

The exhibition centre will be located at Changi and be connected to the island's planned Mass Rapid Transit rail network extension to the airport. Singapore currently has a total of 68,500 sq m (81,930 sq yds) of exhibition space.
